editorial:
Imagine losing your dad and then having to deal with a family that just won't stop picking on you. That is exactly what you get with this heavy hitter of a drama. You follow a teenage boy who is already hurting, but instead of getting a hug, he gets constant insults and pressure from the people who are supposed to love him most. The whole mood is pretty gloomy, and you can really feel the weight of the sadness as the kid starts to slip away. It feels very real, like you are watching a tragedy unfold in a house right down the street from you.

The acting is what really sells it, as the lead actor makes you feel every bit of his pain. While some parts of the story move a bit slow, the emotional payoff is huge and hits you hard. If you enjoy stories about family struggles and mental health, you should definitely give this a shot. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, so I suggest streaming it there for the best picture. If you are a collector, grabbing the 4K Blu-ray for your physical shelf is a great way to keep this powerful story forever.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the boy can no longer handle the mean comments from his family. After a huge fight, he reaches a breaking point that leads to a tragic accident. The final scenes show his family realizing too late how much they hurt him. It ends on a sad note, showing that their words had permanent consequences, leaving the family to live with the guilt of their actions.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional stories about family and growing up.
